films.title: HOCKEY IV
films.description: Hockey's 32-minute fourth full-length builds nine principal parts around the brand's dark, degraded visual language. Its full record preserves five additional documented appearances and a deep 44-person production-credit roll alongside Benny Maglinao's filmmaking credit.
creditNotes: FA WORLD ENTERTAINMENT's authorized complete-film description formally bills nine principal riders and links directly to Hockey's official physical release.
SkateVideoSite independently classifies HOCKEY IV as a 32-minute 2025 full-length, identifies Benny Maglinao, documents five additional appearances and preserves all 44 production contributors.
The 44 production contributors are retained as supported contributor credits without inventing role assignments that the accessible sources do not specify.
locations: New York City, New York, USA
films.locationNote: SkateVideoSite maps the production to Los Angeles and New York City and classifies its country footprint as the United States and France.
films.historicalContext: HOCKEY IV is the brand's fourth numbered full-length and received sustained independent attention, including later Quartersnacks coverage devoted to Ben Kadow's ender and its archival filming record.
films.artworkNotes: The exact authorized upload's 1280x720 YouTube artwork was visually reviewed on 2026-09-17. It uses a dedicated black-and-white HOCKEY IV title composition with no trailer, episode or compilation labeling.

films.title: XXIV
films.description: Habitat Skateboards' 18-minute 24th-anniversary full-length connects 14 riders across a broad North American route. Joe Castrucci leads its edit and art, with travel and individual-part filming credits retained alongside the complete first-party rider order.
creditNotes: Habitat's official complete-film description publishes all 14 skaters in order and role-specific credits for editing, art, travel filming, individual-part filming and still photography.
SkateVideoSite independently classifies XXIV as an 18-minute full-length, corroborates the complete roster, Joe Castrucci's lead credit and the eight-city filming footprint.
No formal director role is inferred; the record preserves only the production roles explicitly published by Habitat.

films.title: DAYDREAM
films.description: Primitive Skate's 27-minute amateur-team full-length centers complete sections from Filipe Mota, Kyonosuke Yamashita and Dylan Jaeb around a 12-rider team montage. Alan Hannon directed and edited the film, with Eric Iwakura and Alex Kissinger sharing principal camera credits.
additionalProductionCredits: Blaine Birardi (motion graphics and art design)
creditNotes: Primitive's official complete-film description identifies the three principal parts, the team montage, Alan Hannon's direction and edit, all three principal filmers, and Blaine Birardi's motion-graphics and art-design credit.

SkateVideoSite independently classifies DAYDREAM as a 27-minute full-length, documents all 15 appearances, corroborates the filmmakers and maps the production to Los Angeles, Toronto, Tokyo and Zürich.
The roster distinguishes the three principal-billed amateur parts from the 12 additional documented team-montage appearances.
films.locationNote: SkateVideoSite independently documents the four-city footprint and identifies Hollywood High School as one of the Los Angeles spots.
films.historicalContext: DAYDREAM introduced a concentrated full-length showcase for Primitive's 2024 amateur class; follow-up unmastered releases and contemporary coverage continued to frame the three principal parts as defining performances for the riders.
films.artworkNotes: The exact official upload's 1280x720 YouTube artwork was visually reviewed on 2026-09-17. It is a dedicated skate photograph without trailer, episode or compilation labeling.
